newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-WARNE TAKES FIVE WICKETS TO ROUT WEST INDIES.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-WARNE TAKES FIVE WICKETS TO ROUT WEST INDIES.

text.p: Australian wrist spinner Shane Warne took five wickets in 15 balls as West Indies collapsed to 161 all out in their World Series limited overs match on Sunday.
West Indies batsman Brian Lara managed to avoid being one of Warne's victims but his failure, his fourth in succession on tour, extended a poor run of form.
Lara, who has yet to score a century since arriving in Australia five weeks ago, struggled for timing on a slow wicket and took 48 balls to score 26 at the Sydney Cricket Ground.
West Indies, who were defeated by Australia in the opening match of the triangular competition on Friday, lost their last six wickets for just 19 runs in the space of 37 deliveries.
Warne dismissed middle order batsman Roland Holder for seven and fast bowler Nixon McLean for a duck in successive deliveries to hasten the tourists' demise in 48.3 overs.
He then repeated the feat in his next over to dismiss wicketkeeper Junior Murray and pace bowler Kenneth Benjamin.
Warne wrapped up the innings by bowling West Indies captain Courtney Walsh for a duck to finish with figures of five for 33.
After scoring at less than two runs an over in the first 10 overs, West Indies relied heavily on Carl Hooper but his team-mates failed to match his contribution of 41 in 58 balls.
Lara, who scored five in Melbourne on Friday, was caught by wicketkeeper Ian Healy after attempting to cut a ball from medium pacer Tom Moody.
